digest.lead: The community is building the infrastructure that AI agents need to be truly useful, with two significant open source projects tackling persistent memory and knowledge management.
digest.summary: Both projects aim to give AI agents the kind of persistent context and knowledge management that users see in Claude.ai, but in open, self-hosted formats.

stories.headline: Developers Launch Open Source Memory Layer to Replicate Claude.ai's Persistent Context
stories.summary: A new open source project called Stash provides a memory layer that allows any AI agent to maintain persistent context across conversations, similar to what Claude.ai and ChatGPT offer [2]. The system aims to give developers the building blocks for creating agents with long-term memory capabilities.
key_points: Provides persistent memory functionality for any AI agent or application
Open source alternative to proprietary memory systems in commercial AI platforms
stories.impact: This could accelerate development of custom AI agents and applications by providing a key missing piece of infrastructure that developers previously had to build from scratch.

sources.title: Open source memory layer so any AI agent can do what Claude.ai and ChatGPT do

stories.headline: New Open Source Project Creates Agent-Maintained Knowledge Wikis Using Git and Markdown
stories.summary: Wuphf is a new open source tool that creates Karpathy-style LLM wikis that AI agents can automatically maintain using Markdown files and Git version control [1]. The project has gained significant traction on Hacker News with strong community engagement.
key_points: Combines familiar developer tools (Git, Markdown) with AI agent automation
Inspired by Andrej Karpathy's approach to LLM documentation and knowledge management
stories.impact: This addresses a growing need for AI agents to maintain and version their own knowledge bases, particularly valuable for development teams and researchers who want transparent, version-controlled AI knowledge systems.

sources.title: Show HN: A Karpathy-style LLM wiki your agents maintain (Markdown and Git)

stories.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
stories.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

stories.headline: Use `/tui fullscreen` for flicker-free Claude Code rendering
stories.summary: The `/tui fullscreen` command switches Claude Code to a flicker-free rendering mode within the same conversation. This improves visual stability and reduces screen flicker during interactions.
actionable_steps: Press Enter to activate flicker-free rendering mode

stories.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
stories.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect

stories.headline: Use the path parameter with EnterWorktree to switch between git worktrees
stories.summary: The EnterWorktree tool now accepts a path parameter that lets you switch into existing worktrees of your current repository. This makes it easier to work with multiple branches or feature development in parallel without switching repositories.
actionable_steps: Identify the worktree path you want to switch to in your current repository
Use the EnterWorktree tool with the path parameter: `EnterWorktree(path="/path/to/your/worktree")`
Verify you're in the correct worktree by checking the current branch or directory

stories.headline: Use defer permission in PreToolUse hooks to pause headless sessions
stories.summary: You can now pause headless Claude Code sessions at tool calls and resume them later with permission evaluation. This allows for better control over automated workflows that need human approval.
actionable_steps: Set up a PreToolUse hook in your Claude Code configuration
Return 'defer' as the permission decision in the hook
The hook will re-evaluate the tool call upon resumption
